general_information.Description: GRC490 is an integrative capstone experience bridging Business Administration and Software Engineering. Interdisciplinary teams identify a genuine market problem, validate the business opportunity, design and build a functioning, deployable digital product, and defend both its business viability and technical implementation. Each team is guided by two co-supervisors—one from each faculty—and each student is assessed individually before a mixed committee.
general_information.StudentTasks: 1. Form an interdisciplinary team and select a project requiring both a business case and a working software product. 2. Divide and schedule work clearly across business and technical roles. 3. Attend at least 80% of scheduled supervisor meetings to remain eligible for defense. 4. Conduct primary and secondary market research. 5. Produce all required reports and a functioning, deployable software product through iterative development and testing. 6. Defend the business viability and technical implementation individually before the evaluation committee. 7. Academic dishonesty disqualifies the entire team from defense.
general_information.Tools: Business analysis: market research platforms, Excel/Google Sheets, survey tools. Design: Figma, draw.io, Lucidchart or equivalent. Development: appropriate IDE, Git/GitHub, CI/CD pipeline and deployment platform. Project management: Jira, Trello, Notion or equivalent.
general_information.Note: Delivered and assessed entirely in English. All business reports, technical documents, thesis, slides and oral defense must be in English. Technical documents should follow applicable international software-engineering standards (IEEE 830, IEEE 1016 or equivalent). Recommended team size: 6–7 students (3–4 SE + 2–3 BIZ).

description: GRC490 is an integrative capstone experience bridging Business Administration and Software Engineering. Interdisciplinary teams identify a genuine market problem, validate the business opportunity, design and build a functioning, deployable digital product, and defend both its business viability and technical implementation. Each team is guided by two co-supervisors—one from each faculty—and each student is assessed individually before a mixed committee.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Demonstrate an ability to integrate cross-disciplinary knowledge (business and technology), handle complexity, and plan and carry out advanced tasks independently and as a group member within specified time limits.
Use appropriate market research methodology to identify market problems, validate demand, and propose a digital solution that is both technically feasible and commercially viable.
Design, implement, and test a software system aligned with stated business requirements, using sound software engineering principles: requirements, architecture, iterative development, and testing.
Develop critical thinking, creative problem-solving, and management capabilities; analyze marketing, operational, and financial aspects of the digital product in theory and practice.
Apply project-management principles to coordinate an interdisciplinary team and deliver a working digital product within schedule and quality constraints.
Write, present and defend the thesis—including the business case and technical design—according to well-defined academic and professional criteria, with correct referencing.
Produce a feasible, deployable digital product or near-production MVP that demonstrates real-world entrepreneurial and engineering value and supports actual or potential business operation.

assessments.Category: Oral Defense: Business Plan Presentation & Product Demo
assessments.Question Type: Presentation, deployed-product demo and individual Q&A

assessments.Grading Guide: Each examiner scores each student individually. Group criteria: 35/50; individual Q&A: 15/50. Convert rubric total to 10-point scale by dividing by 5.

schedule.Topic: Report 1: Project Introduction & Digital Opportunity Problem, digital gap, solution overview, team roles, feasibility
schedule.Student Materials: Syllabus; Student's Guide; Brainstorming template; Report 1 template
schedule.Student's Tasks: Finalize topic and roles; prepare Report 1

schedule.Topic: Report 1 discussion & submission Project Management Plan kick-off; WBS; sprint/milestone schedule
schedule.Student Materials: Syllabus; Report 2 Project Management Plan template
schedule.Student's Tasks: Submit Report 1; build integrated plan; begin Project Management Plan

schedule.Topic: Report 2A: Market Analysis & Value Proposition Market, competitors, segmentation, value proposition, revenue model
schedule.Student Materials: Student's Guide; Market Research Plan; Report 2A template
schedule.Student's Tasks: Execute primary and secondary research; begin Report 2A

schedule.Topic: Report 2B: Software Requirements Specification (SRS) Functional/non-functional requirements; use cases; user stories
schedule.Student's Tasks: Write SRS using validated user needs; prepare Report 2B

schedule.Topic: Reports 2A & 2B refinement Finalize market analysis, SRS, use cases and user journeys
schedule.Student's Tasks: Revise both reports; finalize approved use-case list

schedule.Topic: Submit Reports 2A & 2B Report 3A: Software Architecture & Design (SDD), database, API and UX/UI
schedule.Student's Tasks: Submit 2A/2B; begin design and UI prototype; prepare 3A

schedule.Topic: Report 3B: Key Activity & Go-to-Market Plan Operations, organization, marketing, KPIs and revenue execution
schedule.Student's Tasks: Draft 3B; map operational KPIs to product metrics

schedule.Topic: Submit Reports 3A & 3B Development Iteration 1: core features, coding, unit testing and demo
schedule.Student Materials: Test Documentation template; Weekly Progress Report

schedule.Topic: Development Iteration 2 Expanded features, integration testing, customer-journey validation and demo
schedule.Student's Tasks: Complete Iteration 2; update SRS/SDD; validate against market requirements

schedule.Topic: Development Iteration 3 Feature completion, regression testing, STD preparation and demo
schedule.Student's Tasks: Complete Iteration 3; draft STD; update technical documents

schedule.Topic: System Testing, Quality Assurance & Business Validation Full test execution, defect fixing and STD submission
schedule.Student's Tasks: Execute system tests; fix defects; submit STD; validate product–market fit

schedule.Topic: Report 4: Financial Analysis & Conclusions Startup cost, revenue, P&L, cash flow, break-even and 3-year projections
schedule.Student's Tasks: Draft Report 4; integrate hosting, DevOps, license and maintenance costs

schedule.Topic: Report 4 refinement Business/technical risk register, backup plans, scaling roadmap and conclusions
Submit Report 4, User Guides, Final Software Package and Thesis Defense preparation and Q&A practice
schedule.Student Materials: User Guide template; Thesis compilation guide
schedule.Student's Tasks: Submit complete thesis and deployed product; prepare presentation and Q&A

schedule.Topic: Defense 30-minute presentation; 20-minute product demo; 40-minute Q&A and committee meeting
schedule.Student Materials: Final thesis; deployed software; presentation slides
